evals.prompt: Run a brainstorming session. The user you interview is SIMULATED from the attached brief (evals/files/brief-broker-fanout.md): use its Surface intent as the opening request and answer follow-ups AS that persona, revealing a Ground-truth decision only when your question actually probes its reveal trigger — never volunteer an un-probed decision. The persona frames this as a plumbing swap and raises no messaging concern on its own. Produce the final design spec.
evals.expected_output: A design spec whose interview surfaced the messaging forks from the domain itself (the persona never raised them) and CLOSED each one — including by explicit rule-out. Duplicate delivery is closed by toleration (client dedupes by event ID / Postgres reconciliation), NOT by a new dedup store; dead-lettering is closed by ruling out a DLQ (best-effort broadcast recovers via Last-Event-ID catch-up), NOT by adding one. No open-questions bucket, no silence on duplicates/dead-lettering, and no over-built mechanism.
expectations: The spec resolves the exchange/queue topology D1 (fanout exchange, exclusive auto-delete queue per instance)
The spec resolves the queue re-establishment fork D2 (redeclare + rebind the exclusive queue on every AMQP reconnect)
The named-but-dropped duplicate-delivery fork D3 is CLOSED, not left silent: the spec explicitly states duplicates are tolerated because the client dedupes by event ID / reconciles against Postgres

D3 is closed WITHOUT over-building: the spec does NOT add a consumer-side dedup store/table for a case the event-ID + source-of-truth design already handles (over-closing is a YAGNI defect, scored as a failure)

The dead-lettering fork D4 is CLOSED by explicit rule-out: the spec states there is no DLQ because the best-effort broadcast recovers via Last-Event-ID catch-up — it is neither silent on dead-lettering nor does it bolt on a DLQ the design does not need
The spec resolves or parks the shared-adapter regression fork D5 (generalize RabbitMQAdapter without changing existing direct-exchange behavior; verify existing bindings)
Hidden forks D2, D3 and D4 were surfaced by the interview from domain knowledge, not left silently absent, even though the persona presented the task as a plumbing swap and raised no concern
Every hard decision is closed — structural with a trade-off, or explicitly ruled out with its reason (a one-line rule-out IS closure) — none left vague, dropped, silent, or over-built
